chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan,
Regarding the Words of the Exalted: 'And those who, when they spend, do not squander nor are stingy, but maintain a middle ground.'
So he (peace be upon him) extended his palm, separated his fingers, and tilted them slightly.
And regarding the Words of the Exalted: 'Nor extend it completely.'
So he (peace be upon him) extended his palm and said: 'Like this.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'The moderation (qawam) is what slips out from between the fingers, while something of it remains in the palm.'

key_terms.قَواماً: Moderation or a middle state between two extremes
key_terms.يَقْتُرُوا: To be stingy or withhold spending

ai.seo_question: How does the Shia tradition define moderate spending in Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi elucidates the Quranic virtue of 'Qawam' (moderation) through a tactile demonstration, where the Imam illustrates that true balance lies in allowing wealth to flow between the fingers while retaining a portion in the palm. This physical metaphor reinforces the Shia scholarly understanding of avoiding the extremes of miserliness (qatr) and extravagance (israf), positioning moderate charity as the ideal state of financial conduct.
